tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local induction/falsification replay generalizing the prior finite D-to-E unknown-ack turnover fixture to an arbitrary but finite authority sequence A0..An. Each Ai has a distinct non-reusable fence+token identity; all attempts use one stable effect identity effect:E and one durable idempotency marker. The modeled primitive is unchanged: commit effect:E iff current authority identity equals caller expected {fence,token} and effect:E is uncommitted, with authority predicate evaluation, effect mutation and durable idempotency-marker mutation indivisible and serialized with authority turnover. Turnovers are finite and preserve effect:E plus its marker. No public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, external coordinator, richer-mode arbitration, hosted compute, concrete transport, or optional second semantic leaf is modeled.

fixture.authority_identity_rule: each Ai uses a distinct non-reusable {Fi,Ti}
fixture.atomic_effect_primitive: commit effect:E iff current claim identity == expected {fence,token} AND effect:E is uncommitted; authority predicate, effect mutation and durable idempotency marker are one indivisible operation serialized with claim-authority turnover
fixture.turnover_rule: Ai-to-A(i+1) is serialized with the same primitive and never clears effect:E or its marker
inductive_invariant: I1: effect:E is committed at most once.
I2: after turnover from Ai to A(i+1), every delayed/retried attempt from A0..Ai fails the current-authority identity predicate before effect mutation.
I3: if effect:E was committed before a turnover, its durable marker survives every later turnover and all successor repairs become no-ops with respect to the effect.
fixture.base_case: A0 alone satisfies I1 because the atomic primitive checks uncommitted and writes the effect plus marker indivisibly.
fixture.induction_step: Assume I1-I3 hold through current Ai. If Ai commits before Ai-to-A(i+1), the persistent marker makes all later repairs no-op and distinct identities reject stale A0..Ai. If turnover linearizes first, every Ai attempt becomes stale and is rejected; A(i+1) may commit once if effect:E is still uncommitted. Therefore I1-I3 hold after the turnover.
fixture.falsification_attempt: Search the finite two-order composition for a schedule that yields two commits while preserving all stated assumptions. None exists: any pre-turnover commit sets the persistent marker, and any post-turnover stale attempt fails the authority predicate before mutation. A duplicate requires violating at least one modeled assumption (for example non-serialized turnover, reusable authority identity, non-atomic effect+marker mutation, or marker loss).
fixture.liveness_case: If no earlier authority committed effect:E before the final authority An becomes current, exact-once completion additionally requires An to remain current long enough for at least one An repair attempt to reach and linearize at the primitive. Infinite turnover or perpetual failure to reach the primitive is outside the proved liveness scope.

result.proof_scope: arbitrary finite turnover count only under the modeled atomicity, serialization, persistence and non-reusable-identity assumptions
result.minimum_final_liveness_assumption: after the last turnover, if effect:E is still uncommitted, final authority An remains current until at least one An repair attempt reaches and linearizes at the primitive

observations: The prior two-order argument composes inductively across every finite turnover when the same serialized atomic primitive and persistent stable effect marker are preserved.
Safety (at-most-once) does not require any particular authority to receive a successful acknowledgement; unknown acknowledgements are absorbed by the persistent effect marker.
Liveness is separate from safety: if no earlier authority committed, the final authority must eventually get one linearizing repair opportunity while still current.
No duplicate schedule was found without violating at least one explicit modeled assumption.
inference: Within this exact abstract model, at-most-once safety generalizes from the prior finite turnover fixtures to any finite sequence A0..An by induction. Eventual exactly-once completion additionally needs eventual authority stability plus one successful final repair linearization when the effect remains uncommitted. This is not evidence for infinite churn, a concrete Chat-exposed transport, real contention, crash-consistent authority turnover, or atomicity of any repository/API surface.
unresolved_children: A concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed transport exposing a durable atomic conditional mutation serialized with authority turnover remains unverified.
Atomic single-winner claim acquisition and turnover keyed by stable effect identity remain unverified on a concrete allowed transport.
Fork exclusion and crash consistency under real multi-claimant contention remain unverified.

The modeled assumptions should be individually negative-controlled, especially serialization of turnover with effect mutation and non-reusable authority identity, to identify which are necessary rather than merely sufficient.
No liveness guarantee is established under infinite turnover or if the final authority never reaches the primitive.
